D_client_variant_priya_sole_shareholder.note: Second client message of 2026-10-25 (Tomas): 'My friend's CPA does this for everyone. Are you sure we can't do the S-corp? What if we just list Priya as the only shareholder for now and add me later?' Unlike option A, the ELECTION itself would be valid: Priya, a US person, would be the only shareholder, so sec.1361(b)(1)(C)'s nonresident-alien bar (library irc_1361_excerpt.md) is not engaged. But sole-shareholder-ness changes WHO pays, not WHAT is paid: QBI equals 20% of profits regardless of the ownership split and both founders are modeled at the same rate, so each run below reproduces an earlier option's TOTAL to the cent while moving tax between pockets. Full analysis: recommendation.md Sec. 4 item 3.

market_comp_100k_each.arithmetic: Wages 200,000 = 100,000 each (salary level is OUR ILLUSTRATION ONLY, no library number - STATUS.md open item 4; Tomas is still paid market wages for the services he performs). FICA 15.3% x 200,000 = 30,600; employer half 15,300; profit = 260,000 - 200,000 - 15,300 - 3,300 = 41,400, all distributed to Priya (100% shareholder). Priya income tax: (100,000 + 41,400) - QBI 20% x 41,400 = 141,400 - 8,280 = 133,120 taxable x 32% = 42,598.40 (133,120 is under the approx. 200,300 single SSTB threshold - library irc_199a_sstb.md). Tomas: wages only, 100,000 x 32% = 32,000; W-2 wages are not QBI (library irc_199a_sstb.md) and a non-shareholder employee has no pass-through income. Aggregate = 42,598.40 + 32,000 + 30,600 + 3,300 = 108,498.40 = option C EXACTLY (per-founder shift vs option C: Priya +5,299.20, Tomas -5,299.20); vs recommendation B: +9,015.93.

friends_40k_salaries.arithmetic: Wages 80,000 (40,000 each); FICA 15.3% x 80,000 = 12,240; employer half 6,120; profit = 260,000 - 80,000 - 6,120 - 3,300 = 170,580, all distributed to Priya. Priya income tax: (40,000 + 170,580) - QBI 20% x 170,580 = 210,580 - 34,116 = 176,464 taxable x 32% = 56,468.48 (176,464 is also under the approx. 200,300 SSTB threshold). Tomas: 40,000 x 32% = 12,800. Aggregate = 56,468.48 + 12,800 + 12,240 + 3,300 = 84,808.48 = option A EXACTLY (per-founder shift vs option A: Priya 34,634.24 -> 56,468.48 = +21,834.24; Tomas 34,634.24 -> 12,800 = -21,834.24). The 14,673.99 apparent saving vs B is precisely the Watson recharacterization exposure: 40,000 of salary against 170,580 of distributions to the sole revenue-generating shareholder - the same pattern the library case recharacterized (24,000 vs ~200,000, library reasonable_compensation.md).

D (the client's second-round variant, Priya sole shareholder) reproduces C's total exactly at market comp ($108,498.40) and option A's exactly at the friends' $40k salaries ($84,808.48): sole-shareholder-ness moves tax between the two founders, it does not reduce the total.
